s1.syndrome_frame: Palpitations in a pregnant woman with regular narrow QRS tachycardia
salient_findings: Regular cannon waves on jugular venous pulsations
key_facts: Patient is a primigravid woman in her 20s
Patient is in the eighth month of gestation
Palpitations are nonexertional and episodic
Palpitations last for a few minutes and subside spontaneously
No associated sweating, syncope, dyspnoea, orthopnoea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea
Blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg
Heart rate is 120 beats/min
Jugular venous pulsations reveal regular cannon waves
Auscultation is significant for a variable first heart sound
Laboratory tests are within normal limits
2-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography shows good biventricular function and normally functioning valves
ECG shows regular narrow QRS tachycardia with a ventricular rate of 103-125 beats/min

shortlist.label: atrial tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: regular narrow QRS tachycardia with a ventricular rate of 103-125 beats/min

shortlist.label: atrial fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: irregular heart rhythm suggested by variable first heart sound and regular cannon waves

shortlist.label: atrioventricular dissociation
shortlist.why_kept: regular cannon waves and variable PR intervals on ECG

shortlist.label: supraventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: regular narrow QRS tachycardia and palpitations in a pregnant woman

shortlist.label: ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: wide range of heart rate and presence of cannon waves

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG shows regular narrow QRS tachycardia with a ventricular rate of 103-125 beats/min, and the presence of regular P waves marching onto QRS complexes with varying PR intervals is consistent with supraventricular tachycardia.

rejected.label: atrial fibrillation
rejected.why: Atrial fibrillation is characterized by irregularly irregular rhythm, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: atrioventricular dissociation
rejected.why: Atrioventricular dissociation is characterized by a lack of association between P waves and QRS complexes, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: ventricular tachycardia
rejected.why: Ventricular tachycardia is characterized by wide QRS complexes, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: atrial tachycardia
rejected.why: Atrial tachycardia is a possible diagnosis, but the presence of regular P waves with varying PR intervals and the clinical presentation are more consistent with supraventricular tachycardia.
